card.name: Mid-clause modifiers before a predicted noun
card.fires_on: Small modifier or linking words in the middle of a clause, such as too, very, new, or, at, where a specific noun or phrase is expected next. Most often seen after 'stabilized at a' in liver-test restart instructions.

modes.label: New baseline wording
modes.description: The word 'new' in 'stabilized at a new baseline value' in liver-test hold and restart instructions.
modes.example: total bilirubin levels have either returned to baseline or stabilized at a<< new>> baseline value.

modes.label: General prose modifiers
modes.description: Adverbs or conjunctions such as too, very, or in everyday web text, just before the phrase continues.
modes.example: But sometimes canned<< or>> frozen is a better choice, especially when

modes.label: Clause connectors in drug text
modes.description: Short words like at or it in the middle of a clause in dosing or administration text.
modes.example: until blood pressure has stabilized for<< at>> least an additional hour

card.writes: No clear output effect; the promoted tokens are mixed (paragraph break, folded, neatly, round).
card.plain: It fires on small in-between words in the middle of a sentence, most clearly the word 'new' in 'a new baseline value'.
